positiveFlows.title: THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO COMBINE FIELD, LABORATORY AND MODELING ACTIVITIES TO ANALYZE BIOSOLIDS AND PER AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) CONTAMINATION, PFAS FATE AND TRANSPORT FROM AGRICULTURAL IRRIGATION, THE OCCURRENCE OF PFAS PRECURSORS IN LAND-APPLIED BIOSOLIDS IN LAB STUDIES, OBSERVING INTERFACIAL ADSORPTION TECHNIQUES IN PFAS TRANSPORT, AND MODELING LEACHING RISK TO SURFACE AND GROUND WATER. THE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON ADDRESSING KEY DATA GAPS IN THE UNDERSTANDING OF OCCURRENCE AND FATE OF PFAS IN RURAL AND AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPES.

THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP IMPROVED AND COST-EFFECTIVE TREATMENT TRAINS WITH ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE REMOVAL OF PFASS (PER AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES) FROM DRINKING WATER, WASTEWATER AND BIOSOLIDS FOR SAFE DRINKING WATER. THE PROJECT AIMS TO PRODUCE A NEW AND IMPROVED DATA SET ON ADVANCED TREATMENT PROCESSES TO FILL IN CRITICAL DATA AND KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN TREATMENT TRAINS BY COLLECTING AND CHARACTERIZING THE EFFICIENCY OF PFAS REMOVAL FOR EACH TREATMENT TRAIN FROM SAMPLES ALL ACROSS THE COUNTRY.

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO 1) CHARACTERIZE THE OCCURRENCE, FATE, AND TRANSPORT OF BIOSOLID-ASSOCIATED ORGANIC COMPOUNDS (BOCS) AFTER LAND APPLICATION OF BIOSOLIDSAND 2) MODEL BOC EXPOSURES AND PERFORM HAZARD AND RISK ASSESSMENTS TO IDENTIFY HIGH-PRIORITY BOCSAND AND 3) UTILIZE AN ARRAY OF COMMUNICATION CHANNELS TO TRANSLATE RESEARCH FINDINGS AND METHODOLOGY. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COMBINING LABORATORY AND FIELD EXPERIMENTS TO CHARACTERIZE THE OCCURRENCE AND TRANSFORMATION OF BOCS IN BIOSOLIDS-AMENDED SOILS, ASSESS THEIR POTENTIAL TO CONTAMINATE SURFACE AND GROUNDWATER, AND QUANTIFY BIOACCUMULATION INTO AND METABOLISM WITHIN EDIBLE PRODUCE. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE A NEW, FLEXIBLE FRAMEWORK FOR THE IDENTIFICATION OF HIGH-PRIORITY BOCS IN BIOSOLIDS, WHICH CAN FORM THE BASIS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONS AND DEVELOPMENT OF BEST RISK MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AIMED AT PROTECTING PUBLIC HEALTH AND ECOSYSTEMS. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, WASTEWATER AND AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC AFFECTED BY BOCS.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS RESEARCH IS TO (1) FILL THE KNOWLEDGE GAPS ON THE OCCURRENCE, FATE, TRANSPORT, AND PLANT UPTAKE OF PHARMACEUTICALS AND PERSONAL CARE PRODUCTS (PPCPS) AND PER- AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFASS) AT THE NEXUS OF BIOSOLIDS, SOIL, WATER, AND CROPS VIA PERFORMING SYSTEMATICALLY DESIGNED LABORATORY AND FIELD EXPERIMENTS, (2) INTEGRATE THE DATA TO DEVELOP QUANTITATIVE MODELS FOR EVALUATING HUMAN EXPOSURE THROUGH BIOSOLIDS APPLICATION PATHWAY, AND (3) COMMUNICATE THE RESEARCH RESULTS THROUGH EXTENSION ACTIVITIES.  DIRECT BENEFICIARIES OF THIS PROGRAM INCLUDE THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY, LOCAL AND REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AGRICULTURAL COMMUNITIES, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC AFFECTED BY PFASS AND PPCPS. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE DATA AND USER-FRIENDLY MODELS USEFUL FOR EVALUATING OCCURRENCE, FATE, TRANSPORT, AND PLANT UPTAKE OF PPCPS AND PFASS RELEASED FROM BIOSOLIDS, AS WELL AS A FIELD GUIDE SUMMARIZING RISK FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO HUMAN EXPOSURE TO PPCPS AND PFASS FROM BIOSOLIDS APPLICATION. THE EXPECTED OUTCOME IS A DECREASE IN ASSOCIATED PUBLIC HEALTH AND ECOSYSTEM RISKS.  COLORADO STATE U. positiveFlows.title: DESCRIPTION:THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO ACCELERATE WATER REUSE ADOPTION IN RURAL COMMUNITIES BY INCREASING TECHNICAL AND COMMUNITY READINESS. THE GENERAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT COMMUNITY READINESS FOR WATER REUSE IN SMALL SYSTEMS CAN BE ACCELERATED BY A CONVERGENCE OF TECHNICAL, INFORMATIONAL, SOCIAL, AND INSTITUTIONAL INNOVATION.ACTIVITIES:THE RESEARCH PROJECT AIMS FOR AN INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM THAT WILL: (1) ADDRESS KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND GENERATE FRAMEWORKS FOR OVERCOMING THESE BARRIERS, AND (2) USE RESEARCH OUTPUTS TO EVALUATE AND ACCELERATE COMMUNITY READINESS FOR REUSE IN FIVE CASE STUDIES. BOTH GENERAL ACTIVITIES WILL BE EXECUTED IN PARALLEL SUCH THAT KNOWLEDGE CAN BE CO-PRODUCED WITH DECISION-MAKERS. SPECIFIC METHODS TO ADDRESS KNOWLEDGE GAPS INCLUDE, COMMUNITY SURVEYS, THE USE OF A PROTOTYPE CALCULATION ENGINE, AND DESKTOP, BENCH-SCALE AND PILOT-SCALE EVALUATIONS OF TREATMENT TECHNOLOGIES. SPECIFIC METHODS TO ACCELERATE COMMUNITY READINESS INCLUDE LEGAL AND POLICY ANALYSES AND CASE-STUDY EVALUATIONS OF FIVE SMALL WATER SYSTEMS.SUBRECIPIENT:THE SUBAWARD TO THE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND (REQUESTED $681,965 COST SHARE: $171,319) IS FOR ANALYSES FOR OBJECTIVES 2 (DEVELOP VALIDATED LIST OF FIT-FOR-PURPOSE TECHNOLOGIES), 4 (IDENTIFY WAYS TO OVERCOME SOCIAL BARRIERS TO PUBLIC ACCEPTANCE), AND 6 (CONDUCT CASE STUDIES). THE SUBAWARD TO THE UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA BERKELEY (REQUESTED: $559,941) IS FOR WORK ON ORGANIZATIONAL BARRIERS IN OBJECTIVE 5 (FOSTER INSTITUTIONAL INNOVATION TO OVERCOME ORGANIZATIONAL BARRIERS) AND SUPPORT FOR OBJECTIVE 6 (CONDUCT CASE STUDIES).OUTCOMES:THIS PROJECT'S OUTPUTS INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS, AS WELL AS MODULAR, DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS SUCH AS WATER INVENTORIES, TECHNOLOGY DATABASES, COST AND DEMAND CURVES FOR WATER REUSE. THESE OUTPUTS WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO INSTITUTIONAL AND STATE AND LOCAL REGULATORY DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES IN SMALL, RURAL, AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE STAKEHOLDERS IN SMALL COMMUNITIES SUCH AS UTILITIES AND LOCAL RESOURCE MANAGERS, STATE AND TRIBAL DECISION MAKERS, AS WELL AS CUSTOMERS OF SMALL WATER SYSTEMS.

positiveFlows.title: DESCRIPTION:THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A STATE-WIDE STRATEGY TO ADDRESS PFAS-CONTAMINATED SOILS AND GROUNDWATER AT MULTIPLE SITES AROUND THE STATE OF ALASKA. TO SUPPORT THIS OBJECTIVE, THE RESEARCHERS PLAN TO INVESTIGATE THE AVAILABLE TECHNOLOGIES FOR TREATING PFAS-CONTAMINATED SOILS AND THEIR APPLICABILITY TO ALASKA'S EXTREME ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS, AS WELL AS THE NEEDS OF REMOTE COMMUNITIES TRYING TO ADDRESS PFAS-CONTAMINATED SITES. THIS INVESTIGATION IS EXPECTED TO INCLUDE LABORATORY STUDIES ON HOW FREEZE/THAW CYCLES AFFECT THE EFFICACY OF CURRENTLY AVAILABLE TREATMENT TECHNOLOGIES. ALASKA CURRENTLY LACKS THE ANALYTICAL CAPABILITY TO MEASURE PFAS IN ENVIRONMENTAL MEDIA. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO CREATE A PFAS-FOCUSED LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA, FAIRBANKS. ACTIVITIES:THE RESEARCHERS WILL: (1) EVALUATE EFFECTIVE PFAS CONTAMINATED SOIL AND GROUNDWATER TREATMENT OPTIONS FOR USE IN ALASKA; (2) WORK WITH STATE AGENCIES TO DEVELOP A STRATEGY FOR TREATING PFAS-CONTAMINATED SOIL, SURFACE WATER, AND GROUNDWATER IN URBAN AND REMOTE AREAS IN ALASKA; AND (3) ESTABLISH A LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF) IN THE WATER AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH CENTER (WERC) FOR ANALYSIS OF SOIL AND WATER FOR PFAS COMPOUNDS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS FROM THIS PROJECT INCLUDE A STRATEGY FOR REMEDIATING PFAS CONTAMINATED SOIL AND GROUNDWATER IN ALASKA AND A NEW LABORATORY HOUSED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS DEDICATED TO ANALYSIS OF PFAS COMPOUNDS AND OTHER EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS.. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED HEALTH AND ENVIRONMENT IN THE STATE OF ALASKA. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE ALASKA RESIDENTS, STATE AND LOCAL ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGERS, AND COMMUNITIES FACING SIMILAR CHALLENGES MEASURING PFAS.

DESCRIPTION:THE GOAL OF THE PROJECT TO CONDUCT RESEARCH THAT SUPPORTS COMMUNITY AND HOUSEHOLD RESILIENCE TO WILDFIRE SMOKE THROUGH ACTIONS THAT MITIGATE ADVERSE HEALTH OUTCOMES ASSOCIATED WITH WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURES.ACTIVITIES:THE PROJECT WILL APPLY PRACTICE-DRIVEN APPLIED RESEARCH WITH OREGON COMMUNITIES AND PARTNERS. THE RESEARCH TEAM WILL FACILITATE INFORMATION SHARING AND NETWORKS BETWEEN PRACTITIONERS, MANAGERS, AND RESEARCHERS TO ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE INFORMATION GAPS AND NEEDS OF PRACTITIONERS ON THE GROUND AND TO ACCELERATE THE EFFECTIVE DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH FINDINGS INTO PRACTICE. THE TEAM WILL DISSEMINATE RESEARCH CONDUCTED BY THE CENTER AND PARTNERS TO SPECIFIC AUDIENCES OF INTEREST, THROUGH WEB-BASED APPLICATIONS, TECHNICAL REPORTS, SHORT FACT SHEETS, INFOGRAPHICS, PRESENTATIONS, AND OTHER FORMS OF ACCESSIBLE INFORMATION SHARING.

SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL RESEARCH REPORTS AS WELL AS JOURNAL ARTICLES AND BRIEFING PAPERS DOCUMENTING THE ACTIVITIES AND FINDINGS FROM THE PROJECT. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED ABILITY OF OREGONIANS' TO PREPARE FOR, RESPOND TO, AND RECOVER FROM WILDFIRE SMOKE EVENTS IN ORDER TO REDUCE ADVERSE HEALTH OUTCOMES ASSOCIATED WITH WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURES AS WELL AS NEW KNOWLEDGE AND EFFICACIOUS STRATEGIES THAT OFFER IMPORTANT EVIDENCE-BASED APPROACHES THAT CAN BE APPLIED ACROSS THE WESTERN U.S. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE OREGON RESIDENTS, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.

DESCRIPTION:THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE EXTENT AND SOURCES OF PFAS CONTAMINATION IN WASTEWATER IN DELAWARE. THE RESULTS OF THE RESEARCH WILL HELP IDENTIFY THE MEANS TO PREVENT CONTAMINATION OF DRINKING WATER SUPPLIES.ACTIVITIES:THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO 1) SCREEN WASTEWATER AND SLUDGE FROM SELECTED WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANTS (WWTPS) FOR FLUORINE-CONTAINING ORGANIC CHEMICALS USING TOTAL ORGANO-FLUORINE AND TOTAL PFAS METHODS; 2) QUANTIFY THE AMOUNT OF PFAS IN THE WATER AND SOLID RESIDUE USING THE TARGETED METHOD LC/MS/MS FROM THE SAME WASTEWATER PLANTS; AND 3) COMPARE THE AMOUNTS OF PRECURSORS AND INTERMEDIATES IN THE WASTEWATER AND SLUDGE IN WWTPS AS A FUNCTION OF SEASONAL VARIATIONS.SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DELIVERABLES INCLUDE ANNUAL AND FINAL REPORTS, AS WELL AS GUIDANCE TO WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT (WWTP) OPERATORS AND MANAGERS ABOUT ANALYTICAL METHODS, LEVELS OF PFAS AND OTHER ORGANO-FLUORINE COMPOUNDS AS WELL AS POTENTIAL MITIGATION STRATEGIES SPECIFIC TO THEIR PROCESSES. DIRECT BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE STATE AND LOCAL LEGISLATORS LOOKING TO UNDERSTAND THE EXTENT OF PFAS DISCHARGES INTO THE ENVIRONMENT, DELAWARE RESIDENTS, HUMAN HEALTH, THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC.

positiveFlows.title: DESCRIPTION:THE MAIN OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO HELP ADDRESS HARMFUL ENVIRONMENTAL TRENDS IN THE KODIAK REGION OF ALASKA THROUGH CONTINUOUS PHYTOPLANKTON MONITORING AND BI-WEEKLY SHELLFISH SAMPLING. THE KODIAK AREA NATIVE ASSOCIATION (KANA) HAS IDENTIFIED THE PRESENCE OF THREE DIFFERENT GENUSES OF PHYTOPLANKTON THAT POSE A THREAT TO HUMAN HEALTH AND MARINE MAMMALS, AND ONE OF THEM CAN PRODUCE SAXITOXIN, THE TOXIN RESPONSIBLE FOR PARALYTIC SHELLFISH POISONING (PSP). BECAUSE SOME OF THE HIGHEST TOXIN VALUES IN THE STATE OF ALASKA HAVE BEEN RECORDED IN KODIAK WATERS, TRIBAL MEMBERS AND OTHER KODIAK SUBSISTENCE RESOURCE USERS HAVE STRESSED THE IMPORTANCE OF MONITORING AND RESEARCH THAT WILL HELP REDUCE THEIR RISK OF HARVESTING DURING A PSP EVENT. THIS PROJECT WILL HELP CONTINUE TO ADDRESS ENVIRONMENTAL TRENDS THAT POSE A THREAT TO HUMAN HEALTH AND OTHER MAMMALS UTILIZED AS SUBSISTENCE RESOURCES BY NATIVE AND NON-NATIVE ALASKANS. ACTIVITIES:THIS FUNDING WILL ALLOW KANA TO MONITOR HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS (HABS) IN KODIAK WATERS, COLLECT WEEKLY PHYTOPLANKTON SAMPLES AND REGULAR BI-WEEKLY MONITORING AND TESTING OF SHELLFISH FOR TOXINS THAT COULD CAUSE PARALYTIC SHELLFISH POISONING (PSP). THE RESEARCHERS WILL ALSO COLLABORATE WITH TRIBAL ENVIRONMENTAL STAFF IN VILLAGES AND ON THE KODIAK ROAD SYSTEM ABOUT HABS AND SHELLFISH TESTING. DATA FROM THIS PROJECT WILL BE USED TO CREATE ADVISORIES FOR SHELLFISH HARVESTING AT SEVERAL SAMPLE LOCATIONS ON THE KODIAK ROAD SYSTEM AND IN PARTICIPATING VILLAGES. THE PROJECT IS ALSO DESIGNED TO INCREASE KNOWLEDGE ABOUT HABS AND BIOTOXINS IN KODIAK WATERS AMONG TRIBES AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. SUBRECIPIENT:NO SUBAWARDS ARE INCLUDED IN THIS ASSISTANCE AGREEMENT.OUTCOMES:DATA FROM THIS PROJECT WILL BE USED TO CREATE REGULAR ADVISORIES FOR SHELLFISH HARVESTING AT SEVERAL SAMPLE LOCATIONS ON THE KODIAK ROAD SYSTEM AND IN PARTICIPATING VILLAGES. THE RECIPIENTS ALSO PLAN TO CREATE OUTREACH AND PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENTS, FLYERS, SOCIAL MEDIA POSTS AND OTHER MEANS OF DISSEMINATING THE INFORMATION AND THESE WILL INCLUDE THAT KANA WILL ACCEPT SHELLFISH FROM SUBSISTENCE HARVESTERS AND PROVIDING SHELLFISH TOXIN RESULTS SO THEY CAN MAKE INFORMED HARVEST DECISIONS. THE RECIPIENT WILL SUBMIT ANNUAL REPORTS ON THEIR PROJECT AND FOR THE FINAL REPORT, THEY PLAN TO COLLABORATE WITH KODIAK TRIBES AND THE SITKA TRIBE OF ALASKA ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH LAB (STAERL) TO COMPILE SAMPLES AND ENVIRONMENTAL DATASETS FOR PARALYTIC SHELLFISH POISONING INTO A FINAL REPORT.
